facts.text: The castle, Poggio alle Mura, has a strategic location between Siena and the Maremma.
facts.excerpt: Its strategic location between Siena and the Maremma, and the fertile land surrounding it, have made the Castle of Poggio alle Mura a coveted and hotly contested property for centuries.

facts.text: The castle complex developed mostly between the 9th and 13th centuries, though its origin is earlier.
facts.excerpt: The complex developed mostly between the 9th and 13th centuries, but its origin is certainly earlier.

facts.text: Dungeons dug into the tufa are still visible, and finds from the last restoration suggest a settlement already in Etruscan times.
facts.excerpt: Some dungeons dug into the tufa and still visible, as well as some stone urns and ceramic vessels found during the last restoration, suggest, in fact, the existence of a settlement already in Etruscan times.

facts.text: The Counts Placidi, Sienese nobles, ruled the castle from 1529 until 1959.
facts.excerpt: In 1529, however, the Counts regained possession of the castle and from then on ruled undisturbed until 1959

facts.text: In 1983 the castle became part of the Banfi vineyard estate, and the Mariani family, owners of the winery, restored it after the acquisition.
facts.excerpt: It will be the restoration works desired by the Mariani family - owners of the winery - immediately after the acquisition, bringing it back to its ancient splendor.

facts.text: The fortress has a compact square plan with two inner courtyards and a crenellated watchtower on the northern flank.
facts.excerpt: It has a compact square plan layout and two inner courtyards with a crenellated tower used as a watchtower toward the northern flank.

facts.text: Notable features include the fifteenth-century courtyard with low arches on octagonal pillars and, outside, a rare and ancient mound-shaped ice-house.
facts.excerpt: Of particular interest are the fifteenth-century courtyard, with low arches on octagonal pillars, and, outside, the rare and ancient ice-house, with its characteristic mound shape.

facts.text: Castello Banfi comprises the hotel, two restaurants, the Enoteca, the Balsameria and the Glass Museum.
facts.excerpt: The Hotel, the two Restaurants, the Enoteca, the Balsameria and the Glass Museum.

facts.text: Public tours of the winery last about an hour and are followed by a wine pairing lunch at La Taverna or a wine tasting at L'Enoteca.
facts.excerpt: The tour takes place in groups with other visitors and lasts about an hour and is followed by a wine pairing lunch at La Taverna restaurant or a wine tasting at L’Enoteca.

facts.text: Guests on the public tour need their own car to follow the guide from the castle to the winery, which is 4 km away.
facts.excerpt: You will need your own car to follow the guide from the Castle to the Winery, which is 4 km away.

facts.text: Advance reservation is mandatory for the public tours.
facts.excerpt: Advance reservation is mandatory.

facts.text: The private Discovering Excellence Tour covers vineyards, the wine cellar and an exclusive tasting.
facts.excerpt: Vineyards, wine cellar, exclusive tasting and much more.A unique visit with which you will be guided on a journey through the places and excellences that characterise Castello Banfi.

facts.text: La Sala dei Grappoli is described as the estate's starred restaurant.
facts.excerpt: Dinner at our starred restaurant La Sala dei Grappoli

facts.text: The wine bar inside the Enoteca pairs Banfi wines with Tuscan fare such as platters of local cured meats and cheeses.
facts.excerpt: Located inside the Enoteca, the experience offers a tasting where Banfi wines meet typical Tuscan fare with platters of local cured meats and cheeses

facts.text: Wines that can be tasted include Brunello di Montalcino, Bolgheri, Chianti, Chianti Classico, SuperTuscans and whites, plus Piedmont wines.
facts.excerpt: From Brunello di Montalcino, to Bolgheri, Chianti, Chianti Classico, SuperTuscans and whites, as well as the reality of Piedmont with Alta Langa, Gavi, Moscato, are just some of the wines that can be tasted.

facts.text: Around the resort, Val d'Orcia offers trekking, cycling and horseback riding.
facts.excerpt: such as the **lovers of trekking, cycling, and horseback riding** in Val d'Orcia

facts.text: Pienza, the Abbey of Sant'Antimo, Sant'Angelo in Colle, Camigliano, Sasso d'Ombrone and Castiglione d'Orcia are villages to visit while staying at the resort.
facts.excerpt: Pienza, the Abbey of Sant'Antimo, the ancient tower of **Sant'Angelo in Colle, Camigliano, Sasso d'Ombrone**, and the walls of **Castiglione d'Orcia** are just some of the beauties of these villages to visit while staying at Castello Banfi Wine Resort.

facts.text: The Bottle and Glass Museum is in Poggio alle Mura, in a medieval castle.
facts.excerpt: the Bottle and Glass Museum in Poggio alle Mura, located in an authentic medieval castle

facts.text: Castello Banfi was the first winery in the world to receive certifications for environmental, ethical and social responsibility (ISO 14001 and SA 8000).
facts.excerpt: was the first winery in the world to receive certifications for environmental, ethical and social responsibility (ISO 14001 and SA 8000)

facts.text: Castello Banfi is known internationally for its clonal research on the Sangiovese Brunello grape variety.
facts.excerpt: known today internationally for its clonal research on the Sangiovese Brunello grape variety

facts.text: A marble slab on the entrance portal bears notations about work done to the courtyard in 1654.
facts.excerpt: Also noteworthy is the marble slab on the entrance portal, which bears notations about the work done to the courtyard in 1654.

facts.text: The resort is described as equipped with every comfort, for relaxing with a massage or a stroll through the vineyards.
facts.excerpt: recharge your batteries with a relaxing massage or a stroll through the lush vineyards
